correctness.rationale: The twelve complete atomic third-move candidates are derived from all ternary addition atoms with 0,x,y,z, with cancellation equations handled separately. At x nonzero their exceptional collision slopes form exactly thirteen rational ratios; pairwise reduced cross-difference numerators are at most 15, so no changes occur in prime characteristic at least 17. Each large field realizes every exceptional ratio and a generic ratio, and a generic third element exists because at most twelve values are forced. The zero-first-move case has a stable third-element profile. The exact recursive atomic type construction proves the equivalence of all prime groups of order at least 17. Five explicit characteristic sentences and the rank-three collision-avoidance sentence separate the other six classes. The verifier reproduces seven classes at sample primes including 17,19,23 but finite tests are not substituted for the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The seven-class theorem is a natural complete shallow logical classification for the infinite prime cyclic family. It supplies a sharp uniform representative bound 17 and explicit distinguishing formulas; the thirteen-slope structure identifies an arithmetic reason for eventual logical indistinguishability. Its eleven-versus-thirteen sentence supplies a concrete, direct counterexample to a numerical specialization of a published purported lower bound, which makes the result more than an arbitrary finite table or textbook corollary.
